title: Nervous-system organization: brain, spinal cord and nerves
source_evidence: Complete L51–53 captions read through closing activities/farewells; all40 assigned topics located. Inherited partial audit:9sheets162samples26native repeats; author does not claim repeat video-frame or continuous video/audio viewing. Two independently acquired source-owner-licensed imaging references inspected.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach neurons and glia as cellular classes. Caption 02:27 calls a nerve a bunch of whole neurons; define peripheral nerve as bundles of axons plus Schwann/connective/vascular constituents, with cell bodies elsewhere.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach receptor → afferent → CNS integration → efferent → effector as one circuit template. Higher cognition is distributed, not a compulsory stage of every reflex.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach CNS = brain/spinal cord and PNS = nerves/ganglia; native `f0011` confirms a classification tree, not complete anatomical partitions or every CNS–PNS boundary nuance.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach afferent/efferent direction relative to CNS and somatic/autonomic **motor** classification; “voluntary/involuntary” is a heuristic, and visceral afferents are not excluded.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach gross cerebrum/cerebellum/brainstem/diencephalon map with consistent sagittal/lateral orientation; later L52 supplies detail.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach segmental cord and ascending/descending communication, distinguishing cord from vertebral column and peripheral nerve root.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach spinal withdrawal circuit with concurrent ascending sensory branch; native `f0029` **shows** brainward information and later pain experience, so reject caption's categorical “no further processing towards brain.” No universal latency without segment/path/velocity.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach PNS sensory and motor fibers; nerves are mixed or specialized bundles, not all merely commands from CNS.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach somatic motor-terminal acetylcholine at neuromuscular junction (with Chapter 15 linkage). Caption 18:52 overgeneralizes ACh as the molecule passing neuron-to-neuron all the way from brain to muscle; distinguish intermediate synapses.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach sympathetic/parasympathetic outflows with preganglionic ganglionic and postganglionic stages. The slide at `f0041` says “often opposing,” but caption 19:59 says exactly opposite; retain “often” and receptor/organ exceptions.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach enteric circuits within gut wall and autonomic modulation; native `f0041` states independent but influenced, not isolated from CNS.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach organ-specific branch effects and transmitter compartments. Native `f0045/f0049` show a simplistic organ chart. Correct sympathetic preganglionic ACh, common postganglionic norepinephrine and cholinergic sweat-gland exception; adrenal epinephrine is hormonal. Do not equate urination/bladder emptying to renal urine **output**, or claim global parasympathetic vasoconstriction/uterine relaxation.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: **Late activity visible** `f0052`: barking/running dog, identify branch and mediators. Teach threat response as sympathetic activation plus adrenal medullary epinephrine, with ACh at preganglionic synapses and NE at many postganglionic targets. Source `f0051` says 86 billion neurons in *nervous system*; scope the estimate to **brain** and cite its uncertainty.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach approximate adult brain mass and energy needs only with population/measurement denominator; native `f0005` claims 20% of body's “glucose and oxygen,” while literature often states energy/oxygen utilization. Do not conflate hypoglycemia with hypoxia. “86 billion” is brain estimate, not all nervous system.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach skull, dura (cranial periosteal and meningeal), arachnoid, pia and CSF **subarachnoid** space. Native `f0009` verifies labels, but slide is illustrative, not sectional micrograph. Distinguish venous dural sinus, blood vessels and fluid spaces.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach gyrus/sulcus/fissure and cortical folding with schematic surface map. Correct caption “rays/sulky”; folding does not mechanically prove a specific cognitive gain.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach cerebrum, cerebellum, brainstem and diencephalon as a useful gross map; “most primitive/oldest” brainstem is evolutionary shorthand, not a literal unchanged ancestral organ.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach anatomical hemispheres and **task-specific** lateralization within distributed networks. Native `f0024` depicts language often left dominant; caption 12:28 implies left-handed → right-dominant, contradicted by research. Handedness does not determine a person's language hemisphere.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach frontal/precentral motor and prefrontal contributions, with Broca-network language production. Localized labels are not exclusive single-function modules, and “inhibition of inappropriate behavior” likely corrects caption “innovating.”

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach parietal somatosensory and spatial/integration roles, specifying postcentral region and other network connections rather than all skin information confined to one lobe.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach temporal auditory, memory, language and ventral visual contributions. Native `f0034` correctly locates inferior temporal cortex relative to parietal and includes object recognition; caption 16:42 is self-contradictory. Hippocampus/amygdala are deep medial structures, not entire lobe modules.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach occipital visual processing in a distributed ventral/dorsal visual system; face recognition is not simply “in occipital association cortex.”

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach cerebellar coordination/prediction/learning. Native `f0041` says ~10% brain volume and >half neurons; any numbers need method/sample scope. Balance also uses vestibular/brainstem/spinal circuits.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach midbrain/pons/medulla with separate functions and continuation into cord. Native `f0045` labels pons correctly; caption from 22:03 omits its name. Avoid describing each vital function as one isolated center.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach thalamic relay/integration with modality exceptions and hypothalamic autonomic/endocrine coupling. “All sensory information” needs exception for olfaction; hypothalamus is not merely a pituitary precursor gland.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach “limbic system” as a historical distributed functional grouping, not one sharply bounded anatomical unit; native `f0052` lists hippocampus, amygdala, hypothalamus, cingulate and olfactory bulb.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach prolonged maturation and lifelong plasticity. Caption/slide “prefrontal cortex fully developed by mid-20s” is too discrete; specify measured property, population and changing trajectories, not a behavioral cutoff.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: **Late activity visible** `f0054`: skill learning, early vs practiced vs habitual networks. Frame as network and time-scale reasoning, not invented region-specific activation data. Motor skill and language learning need distinct circuits; sleep/practice effects are not read from this slide.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach spinal dura, arachnoid, pia, epidural and CSF-containing subarachnoid spaces. Native `f0006` draws “subdural space” as a gap; in ordinary anatomy it is a **potential** space. It must not be illustrated as a normally patent CSF chamber.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach gray/white matter as relative cellular/axon-myelin composition. Caption claims gray has *no* myelin/fat; source slide says unmyelinated axons but cannot demonstrate absence. This is a composition gradient, not an absolute color test.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach developmental/level-dependent central canal as a **schematic** midline landmark. Slide `f0006` and contact-sheet cross section imply a patent CSF conduit in all adults; an adult-human MRI/histology study finds it absent/occluded in most beyond 18. State species and age explicitly.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach dorsal sensory input, ventral somatic motor output, lateral/intermediate autonomic neurons. Native `f0015` slide correctly places thoracolumbar sympathetic neurons, but caption adds parasympathetic activity to that same lateral-horn group; sacral parasympathetic outflow requires separate segment/site.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach ascending/descending white-matter tracts as selected named examples, with **crossing, modalities and level** qualified. Native `f0019` shows gracilis/cuneatus and other areas; a color spot does not prove a tract position at every cord level.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach twelve conventionally numbered cranial nerve pairs, their major central attachments and PNS/CNS boundary nuance for optic/olfactory structures. Caption calls them all brainstem-origin; CN I/II and spinal component of XI are exceptions.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach dominant sensory/motor/mixed modalities in a CN I–XII table. Native `f0027/f0031` **includes X in mixed group**, despite caption 15:35 enumerating only V,VII,IX; preserve X and parasympathetic components. Labels are simplified, not all fiber classes.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach nerve-specific functions (I smell, II vision, III/IV/VI eye movement, V facial sensation/chewing, VII expression/taste, VIII hearing/balance, IX/X pharynx/viscera, XI neck/shoulder, XII tongue). Native `f0036` visibly says CN VI lateral rectus and VII expression/taste. Correct caption “trigeminal neuralgia” → trigeminal nerve and “swirling” → swallowing.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach **31 pairs** (8 C,12 T,5 L,5 S,1 coccygeal), dorsal sensory root/ganglion + ventral motor root joining a mixed spinal nerve. Native `f0040` includes coccygeal despite caption's earlier four-region list. Nerve is axon bundle, not “coiled whole neurons”; segment and vertebral exit are not identical levels.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach cervical, brachial and lumbosacral plexus redistribution with roots/branches. Native `f0043` source begins cervical at C1–C5, whereas standard cervical plexus often C1–C4 (C5 contribution to phrenic); avoid blanket boundary and organ-to-one-region mapping.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: Teach cranial vs spinal nerve count, origin, function and ganglion comparison as a table with exceptions. Native `f0048` broadly lists 12 vs 31, but “cranial nerves mostly head and neck” has vagus exception, and sensory ganglia are not motor nuclei.

coverage_topics.coverage_status: Located in developed author draft; not review acceptance
coverage_topics.disposition: **Late activity visible** `f0053`: loss of smell, difficulty moving **left** eye laterally, left facial droop. Anatomical candidates: I, left VI, left VII, but signs do not establish a single lesion; smell side unspecified, facial central/peripheral pattern and ocular examination unspecified. The three simultaneous signs could require multiple sites or broader process, so write a localization reasoning solution with uncertainty and no patient diagnosis.

MRI catalogue does not explicitly state species, age,sex or acquisition settings; T1contrast is not naturalcolor or activation.
Rat silver-stain localfield is not adult-human whole-cord evidence or signal kinetics.
Constant-delay graph is original synthetic bookkeeping; no empirical conduction fit, pain-consciousness estimate or clinical diagnosis.
Sourceframe audit inherited and partial; no new continuous source video/audio viewing.
Primary studies accessed at stated abstract/relevant-passage depth; no fabricated fullmethods access.
